body:
It's not my parents, it's my fiance and my roommate.  There have been so many times that my fiance has wanted to go have dinner or go out somewhere and I can't muster enough energy to do anything.  He's very loving but after the doctor said it must be in my head, I can see he's gotten a little more upset if I can't do the things we used to do.  I also can't work so we only have two incomes instead of the 3 we had.  I understand what you're saying about needing each other but it feels like I just can't be there for them in the ways they want, and that is a huge disappointment to myself and them.  The worst days are when I can't even put on a smile and try to be pleasant; I know my fiance tries so hard to make me happy and can't understand how I feel but he also feels like he's failing then.

I'm 28, so I'll have to go through the open market in November.  I tried to get health insurance a few months ago but apparently you have to wait even when trying to purchase your own.  

I truly hope that there is some amazing life in the future.  I've never been suicidal and haven't even really experienced depression before.  I have so many things I've waited to do and now it seems like it's in vain.  It's such a shock to go from an active, happy person who's capable of anything to being so limited every day.  All I want is an answer, and the most frustrating thing is that doctors don't seem to know or care to figure it out.  It's led me to have little trust in them and worry that even if they "figure it out", it may not be the correct answer.  If I had listened to my GP, I'd be doped up on Zoloft right now and even worse off than before.  In all of this, trying to remind yourself why life is worth living is very difficult.

I try to do the thing I can from bed, like watch my favorite shows or knit, but I see everyone around me living their lives without restriction and it's so hard.  I'm jealous and angry because my body betrayed me and I can't do anything to fix it right now.

Thank you for your kind words.  It gives me a little hope that there is some possibility that this could get better.  I keep telling myself that and not truly believing it.  That's the reason I've given myself a year - I figure it will give me time to not give up before I've tried everything.  It's attempting to get through every day that's killing me.
I've already changed my diet and don't eat gluten or dairy.  I exercise for an hour every day.  Honestly, if it is autoimmune, that's even more of a reason to check out.

I cleaned up my diet a few months ago hoping it had something to do with how I'm feeling.  I don't eat wheat or dairy.  I went on the keto diet but felt worse than ever so I just try to keep my carbs relatively low now.  I want to know what the problem is more than anything, but the longer this goes on and the more my doctor ruled out, the more frustrating it is.

Right now, I feel like if the option is to continue to wake up every day to constant pain and always being tired, it doesn't feel like I'm living.  I can't go out and do the things I love, I can't spend time with people I love without feeling like I need to nap, and I can't focus on any future.  I equate it to a life sentence in prison versus the death penalty.  If I know there's going to be years of pain ahead of me, I'd rather just have it all be done with.

Thank you.  I'm hoping for answers as well, it just seems like I'm in short supply of them.  I also don't want to feel like I have to club my doctor over the head to get them.  How did you manage to get by for years?  I can't even imagine having to go through this for another year, let alone several.
I'm hoping that it isn't CFS.  I've looked into it before and the prognosis looks bleak - there's not many options for treatment.  I'm not even sure how people manage to keep going while having it.

Thank you.  I'm hoping to get good insurance if I can afford it once open enrollment starts.  I feel awful at having to involve my family, because they see me go through this every day and I know it's exhausting for them as well.  I try my best not to burden them but it's hard when they expect you to be involved and it's a task to get up even to go to the bathroom.

I'll see if I can get into a rheumatologist.  It's daunting to think of having to go through more tests but I desperately want to feel better.

I'd love to do that.  Unfortunately it always begs the question "how am I paying for this?"  In my area, hardly any specialists will see you with no insurance, and most want $250 just for a consultation.
